name: Starter: French
about: French in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in French order.

words.devoir: must, to have to; devoirs: homework
words.excuser: to excuse; excuse-moi: sorry, excuse me

ca-va.about: Literally that goes: a question with your voice going up, an answer with it going down.

s-il-vous-plait.about: Literally if it pleases you; s'il te plaît to a friend.

concept.line: The verb changes with who does it: je parle (I speak), tu parles (you speak), il or elle parle (he or she speaks), nous parlons (we speak), vous parlez (you speak), ils or elles parlent (they speak).
Ask by raising your voice at the end, or start with est-ce que (is it that).
Every noun is masculine or feminine, and le or la, un or une and the adjectives with it match it: un petit chat, une petite maison.

words.means: j'ai = I have; as = have; n'ai = do not have

concept.line: Where English says I'm hungry, thirsty or twenty, French says I have: J'ai faim (I have hunger), J'ai vingt ans (I have twenty years).

words.means: j'habite = I live; habites = live; habite = lives

concept.line: Most adjectives come after the noun: une maison bleue (a house blue).
Je vais, tu vas, il va and an infinitive say what's going to happen, with no word for to: Je vais manger (I go eat).
